source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN Examination, 7th ed.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: Which emotional need should the nurse anticipate in a client having a precipitous labor?
options: Support in keeping a sense of control
Less pain than in a normal labor
questions.rationale: Because of its abrupt onset and quick progress, precipitous labor makes it hard for the client to keep control. She needs support to understand and adapt to the rapid changes.
explanations: Correct: rapid labor threatens her sense of control.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q970 (PDF p. 1219)
questions.quote: The client experiencing a precipitous labor may have more difficulty maintaining control because of the abrupt onset and quick progression of the labor.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Parents of a newborn with an undescended testicle ask what can happen if it is not corrected. Which complication with a psychosocial impact should the nurse mention?
questions.rationale: The testes need a temperature below body temperature to produce fertile sperm, so uncorrected cryptorchidism can cause infertility. An 'empty scrotum' can also affect self-perception.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q972 (PDF p. 1221)
questions.quote: Infertility can occur in males with this condition because proper function of the testes in producing fertile sperm depends on a temperature of less than 98.6° F (37.0° C).

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: The mother of a newborn with hydrocephalus says, 'I'm not sure I can care for my baby at home.' Which response is MOST therapeutic?
options: 'You're worried about caring for him at home?'
questions.rationale: Paraphrasing restates the mother's message and invites her to share more. The other responses minimize her concern or give false reassurance.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q973 (PDF p. 1222)
questions.quote: Paraphrasing is restating the mother’s message in the nurse’s own words.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: Before an amniotomy, which data is the PRIORITY to assess?
questions.rationale: Fetal well-being must be confirmed before and after amniotomy by checking the FHR with a Doppler or external monitor. Scalp sampling is not possible with intact membranes.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1103 (PDF p. 1387)
questions.quote: Fetal well-being must be confirmed before and after amniotomy.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: At 35 weeks, a client reports a sudden gush of fluid from the vagina without contractions. What should the nurse suspect?
questions.rationale: PROM usually shows as a sudden discharge of vaginal fluid before 37 weeks. Preterm labor shows contractions, cramping, and pressure; miscarriage shows bleeding and pain.
explanations: Presents with loss of fetal movement.
Correct: a sudden gush of fluid.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1108 (PDF p. 1392)
questions.quote: Premature rupture of the membranes is usually manifested by a sudden discharge of fluid from the vagina before 37 weeks of gestation.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: A pregnant client with mitral valve prolapse needs anticoagulation. Which drug and route does the nurse expect?
questions.rationale: Heparin does not cross the placenta, so it is the safe anticoagulant in pregnancy, given subcutaneously. Warfarin crosses the placenta.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1125 (PDF p. 1409)
questions.quote: Heparin, which does not pass the placental barrier, is a safe anticoagulant therapy during pregnancy

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: A postpartum client has thromboembolic disease. Which intervention MOST helps prevent pulmonary embolism?
questions.rationale: Anticoagulants prevent clots from forming and from moving to other areas, so they directly prevent pulmonary embolism. The other measures monitor but do not prevent.
explanations: Correct: prevents clot formation and movement.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1145 (PDF p. 1432)
questions.quote: The purposes of anticoagulant therapy for the treatment of thromboembolytic disease are to prevent the formation of a clot and to prevent a clot from moving to another area

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: A pregnant client is admitted with worsening heart disease. Which diet should the nurse discuss with the dietitian?
options: High in fiber with enough fluids
questions.rationale: Constipation can lead to straining (Valsalva maneuver), which can overload the heart. Adequate fluid and fiber prevent constipation. Low-calorie diets are not used in pregnancy.
explanations: Leads to constipation and low blood volume.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1148 (PDF p. 1435)
questions.quote: Constipation can cause the client to use Valsalva’s maneuver. This maneuver can cause blood to rush to the heart and overload the cardiac system.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: The nursery is told that a newborn of an Rh-negative mother is coming. What should the nurse do first?
options: Get the baby's type and Coombs
questions.rationale: Cord blood taken at delivery gives the newborn's blood type, Rh factor, and direct Coombs test. These results guide care.
explanations: Correct: the results are needed to plan care.
RhoGAM is given to the mother, not the infant.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1172 (PDF p. 1459)
questions.quote: Umbilical cord blood is taken at the time of delivery to determine blood type, Rh factor, and antibody titer (direct Coombs’ test) of the newborn infant.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother Before Birth
questions.stem: In the second trimester, the fetal heart rate is 100 beats per minute. What should the nurse do FIRST?
options: Tell the mother it is slow
questions.rationale: The normal FHR is 120 to 160 bpm. A rate of 100 needs prompt evaluation, so the provider is notified, and the finding is also documented.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1205 (PDF p. 1497)
questions.quote: The FHR should be between 120 and 160 beats/min during pregnancy.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: After a gush of fluid in active labor, the monitor shows variable decelerations with each contraction. What should the nurse do FIRST?
questions.rationale: Variable decelerations after a gush of fluid suggest cord compression from prolapse. A vaginal exam detects the cord and confirms the problem.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1181 (PDF p. 1471)
questions.quote: Variable deceleration with brief acceleration after a gush of amniotic fluid is a common clinical manifestation of cord compression

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: What is MOST important when admitting a newborn with myelomeningocele?
questions.rationale: Increased intracranial pressure is a complication of spina bifida, and a bulging anterior fontanel is a sign of it. Temperature also matters because of infection risk.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1191 (PDF p. 1483)
questions.quote: A sign of intracranial pressure in the newborn infant with spina bifida is a bulging anterior fontanel.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A term infant had hypoglycemia at 1 hour of age. At 24 hours, which finding needs follow-up?
options: Weight loss of 100 g with dry, peeling skin
Glucose of 45 mg/dL before a feeding
A high-pitched cry and poor feeding
questions.rationale: Hypoglycemia causes CNS signs such as a high-pitched cry and weak feeding. Early weight loss and peeling skin are normal.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1216 (PDF p. 1509)
questions.quote: Hypoglycemia causes central nervous system symptoms (high- pitched cry), and it is also exhibited by a lack of strength for eating enough for growth.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: Two days after admission for gestational hypertension, which finding shows the condition is WORSENING?
questions.rationale: Headache or blurred vision means the condition is worsening and needs immediate evaluation. The other findings suggest improvement.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1222 (PDF p. 1515)
questions.quote: Client complaints of headache or blurred vision indicate a worsening of the condition and warrant immediate further evaluation.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: The nurse encourages oral fluids during labor. Which finding shows a successful outcome?
questions.rationale: Specific gravity measures urine concentration, and the kidneys tend to concentrate urine in labor. A specific gravity of 1.020 shows adequate hydration. Ketones show inadequate intake.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1233 (PDF p. 1526)
questions.quote: Urine specific gravity measures the concentration of the urine.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother Following Birth
questions.stem: The goal is 'The client will remain free of infection during her stay.' Which finding BEST shows the goal was met?
questions.rationale: Fever is the first sign of infection, so its absence suggests no infection. A temperature up to 38°C can be normal from the dehydrating effects of labor.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1234 (PDF p. 1527)
questions.quote: Fever is the first indication of an infection.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother Before Birth
questions.stem: Which statement shows a pregnant client understands the purpose of Kegel exercises?
questions.rationale: Kegel exercises strengthen the pelvic floor (pubococcygeal muscle). Pelvic tilts ease backache, and leg elevation reduces ankle edema.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1253 (PDF p. 1553)
questions.quote: Kegel exercises assist in strengthening the pelvic floor (pubococcygeal muscle).

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: Which procedure should be AVOIDED during labor to reduce HIV transmission to the fetus?
questions.rationale: Any procedure that exposes the fetus to maternal blood or body fluids is avoided. Internal scalp electrodes break the fetal skin.
explanations: Not a transmission risk to the fetus.
Correct: exposes the fetus to maternal fluids.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1271 (PDF p. 1572)
questions.quote: Direct (internal) fetal monitoring is a procedure that may expose the fetus to maternal blood or body fluids and therefore should be avoided.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: One hour after surfactant therapy for RDS, which finding shows the newborn is improving?
options: A slight rise in respiratory rate
Arterial pH rising to 7.35 or higher
questions.rationale: RDS causes hypoxemia and metabolic acidosis. An arterial pH rising to 7.35 or more means the acidosis is resolving.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1296 (PDF p. 1597)
questions.quote: If the arterial blood pH increases to ≥7.35, the metabolic acidosis is resolving and the newborn’s condition is improving.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: How should a newborn with gastroschisis be positioned before surgery?
questions.rationale: In gastroschisis the bowel is outside the abdomen with no sac. The infant is kept side-lying with the bowel supported by a blanket roll to prevent vascular compromise, kept NPO on IV fluids.
explanations: Puts pressure on the exposed bowel.
Correct: prevents twisting of the bowel.
The bowel must be covered and protected.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1331 (PDF p. 1633)
questions.quote: The infant should be placed in a side-lying position and the viscera supported with a blanket roll to prevent vascular compromise

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: Ten days postpartum, a breastfeeding mother calls with a red, painful breast and fever. What should the nurse advise?
options: Feed only from the other breast
Call the MD; nurse both sides
Apply ice and skip a feed
questions.rationale: Fever with a red, painful breast suggests mastitis. The provider is notified so an antibiotic safe for the baby can be prescribed. The mother keeps nursing on both breasts, starting with the unaffected one.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1333 (PDF p. 1635)
questions.quote: The mother should continue to nurse on both breasts, but should start the infant on the unaffected breast

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother Before Birth
questions.stem: What is the role of estrogen in pregnancy?
options: Maintains the uterine lining for implantation
Promotes uterine growth and prepares the breasts
questions.rationale: Estrogen stimulates uterine development and prepares the breasts for lactation. Progesterone maintains the uterine lining, hPL converts glucose to fat, and hCG maintains the corpus luteum.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1348 (PDF p. 1651)
questions.quote: Estrogen stimulates uterine development to provide an environment for the fetus and stimulates the breasts to prepare for lactation.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: How should the nurse describe imperforate anus to parents?
questions.rationale: Imperforate anus is incomplete development or absence of the anus in its normal position. Incontinence describes encopresis, and telescoping describes intussusception.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1354 (PDF p. 1657)
questions.quote: Imperforate anus (anal atresia, anal agenesis) is the incomplete development or absence of the anus in its normal position in the perineum.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the Well Child (Neonate to Adolescent)
questions.stem: What is the approximate stomach capacity of a newborn?
questions.rationale: A newborn's stomach holds about 10 to 20 mL. It grows to 30 to 90 mL by 1 week and 75 to 100 mL by 2 to 3 weeks.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1355 (PDF p. 1658)
questions.quote: The stomach capacity of a newborn is approximately 10 to 20 mL.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother Following Birth
questions.stem: Which measure relieves nipple soreness in a breastfeeding mother?
options: Keep the same position to toughen the nipple
Stop nursing on the sore side
Align baby's ear, shoulder, hip, tummy to mother
Pull the baby off without breaking suction
questions.rationale: Comfort measures include proper alignment (ear, shoulder, and hip in line, baby's stomach against the mother's), rotating positions, breaking suction with a finger, nursing often, and starting on the less sore side.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1356 (PDF p. 1659)
questions.quote: Comfort measures for nipple soreness include positioning the infant with the ear, shoulder, and hip in straight alignment

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother Following Birth
questions.stem: Immediately after delivery, where does the nurse expect to find the fundus?
options: At or slightly below the umbilicus, midline
questions.rationale: Right after delivery, the fundus is at the umbilicus or one to three fingerbreadths below it, in the midline. A deviated fundus may mean a full bladder; a high fundus may mean clots.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1358 (PDF p. 1661)
questions.quote: Immediately after delivery, the uterine fundus should be at the level of the umbilicus or one to three fingerbreadths below it and in the midline of the abdomen.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother Following Birth
questions.stem: Two hours after delivery, a mother's temperature is 38.9°C (102°F). What should the nurse do?
questions.rationale: A slight rise from dehydration is normal, but 38.9°C (102°F) suggests infection and is reported to the provider.
explanations: Not enough for this level of fever.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1359 (PDF p. 1662)
questions.quote: A temperature of 102° F indicates infection, and the primary health care provider should be notified.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: After a vaginal delivery with epidural anesthesia, a vaginal hematoma is suspected. Which finding is the BEST indicator?
questions.rationale: Under anesthesia the client cannot feel pain or pressure, so vital sign changes showing hypovolemia are the best indicator. Bruising may simply come from the delivery.
explanations: May come from the delivery itself.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1360 (PDF p. 1663)
questions.quote: Changes in vital signs indicate hypovolemia in the anesthetized postpartum woman with a vaginal hematoma.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: What is the PRIORITY assessment for a postterm small-for-gestational-age newborn?
questions.rationale: Hypoglycemia is the most common metabolic complication in SGA newborns and can cause CNS damage if not corrected immediately.
explanations: Correct: hypoglycemia is the main risk.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1362 (PDF p. 1665)
questions.quote: The most common metabolic complication in the SGA newborn is hypoglycemia

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A newborn with Apgar scores of 1 and 4 is coming to the nursery. What is the PRIORITY?
questions.rationale: With low Apgar scores, keeping the airway open comes first, so respiratory resuscitation equipment is prepared. The other measures are lower priority.
explanations: Correct: the airway and breathing come first.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1364 (PDF p. 1667)
questions.quote: The top priority action for a newborn infant with low Apgar scores is maintaining a patent airway

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother Following Birth
questions.stem: Which measure relieves breast engorgement in a breastfeeding mother?
options: Warm compress or shower before feeding
Skip feedings to let breasts rest
questions.rationale: Comfort measures include massaging the breasts before feeding, alternating breasts, a warm shower or compress just before feeding, and a supportive bra at all times.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1414 (PDF p. 1720)
questions.quote: taking a warm shower or applying warm compresses just before feeding, and wearing a supportive well-fitting bra at all times.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother Before Birth
questions.stem: Which statement by a woman reflects a PRESUMPTIVE sign of pregnancy?
options: 'I haven't had a period in 2 months.'
questions.rationale: Presumptive signs are subjective changes the woman experiences: amenorrhea, nausea and vomiting, breast changes, urinary frequency, fatigue, and quickening.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1465 (PDF p. 1774)
questions.quote: the presumptive signs of pregnancy are nausea, vomiting, breast changes, amenorrhea, urinary frequency, fatigue, and quickening.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: Pressing on a prenatal client's shin leaves a pit about 1 inch (2.5 cm) deep. How should the nurse document it?
questions.rationale: A pit about 1 inch deep is +4 edema. A slight pit is +1, about 1/4 inch is +2, and about 1/2 inch is +3.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1537 (PDF p. 1848)
questions.quote: An indentation approximately 1-inch deep would be indicative of +4 edema.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: A client at 30 weeks in preterm labor receives betamethasone. What is its purpose?
options: To keep the ductus arteriosus open
questions.rationale: Betamethasone increases surfactant and fetal lung maturity, reducing respiratory distress syndrome. Surfactant is not stable until after 32 weeks.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1547 (PDF p. 1859)
questions.quote: Betamethasone, a corticosteroid, is administered to increase the surfactant level and increase fetal lung maturity
